source_claim: A paper's explicitly evidenced claim-bearing operator can be compiled into an outcome-blind, same-scaffold operator-versus-sham trial that reports only its cost-adjusted local effect on one independently locked user task.

axes.problem: Rapidly test whether the core mechanism of a paper helps on the user's current task without reproducing the complete paper.
axes.mechanism: Source-map operator selection, a paper-named baseline, interface-identical execution branches, a frozen independent scorer, and an abstaining paired local-effect interval.
axes.insight: Whole-skill or whole-paper comparisons entangle the claimed operator with scaffolding; a task-local operator contrast can identify a narrower effect without predicting future adoption utility.
axes.application: Paper-derived agent methods and user-supplied locked tasks.
axes.evaluation_scope: Separate task case studies with paired seeds, factor-integrity gates, local score, cost, guardrail regressions, and inconclusive outcomes.

comparisons.title: A Framework for Evaluating Agentic Skills at Scale
comparisons.evidence: The framework measures the same agent-model configuration with and without a skill on skill-derived tasks; it does not compile one paper-evidenced operator and its named baseline into an interface-identical trial on a task frozen before paper inspection.
comparisons.limitations: It already defeats broad novelty claims about first marginal utility evaluation for agent skills.

comparisons.title: PaperBench: Evaluating AI's Ability to Replicate AI Research
comparisons.evidence: PaperBench separately scores code development, execution, and result matching for complete paper replication; it does not construct a task-local operator intervention and sham.
comparisons.limitations: It defeats any claim that LocalClaim is the first rapid or decomposed paper-reproduction evaluation.

comparisons.title: AutoReproduce: Automatic AI Experiment Reproduction with Paper Lineage
comparisons.evidence: AutoReproduce constructs and validates end-to-end experiments with mini-batch and dry-run checks, not an outcome-blind operator-specific local-effect contrast.
comparisons.limitations: Its automated lineage and executable checks are strong baselines for the compilation portion.

comparisons.title: Dimension-Level Intent Fidelity Evaluation for Large Language Models: Evidence from Structured Prompt Ablation
comparisons.evidence: The available excerpt uses structured ablation to isolate prompt dimensions, a direct ancestor of component-specific intervention, but does not establish automated paper-operator compilation or a task-local net-effect contract.
comparisons.limitations: Only a partial method/results excerpt is available in the local cache.

comparisons.title: SkillFoundry: Automated Mining and Validation of Agent Skills for Scientific Tasks
comparisons.evidence: SkillFoundry mines operational contracts, validates them, and evaluates downstream utility, but does not isolate a paper-named operator against an interface-identical sham selected without outcome access.
comparisons.limitations: The overlap makes the operator-compiler and same-scaffold contrast the only defensible delta.

limitations: Candidate-specific external collision terms were not transmitted; the assessment reuses generic run-scoped searches.
Classical randomized component ablation is a high-risk ancestor and must not be claimed as novel.
The eight existing tasks support bounded case studies, not cross-task or cross-paper generalization.
